chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Baghdady narrated that Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Suleiman ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hassan quoted his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Zayd ibn Ali, on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family):

He said: The Honorable the Exalted God has created one hundred thousand Prophets and twenty-four thousand Prophets, and I am the dearest of them to God and I do not boast. The Honorable the Exalted God has created one hundred thousand Trustees and twenty-four thousand Trustees, so Ali is the dearest of them to God and the best of them.
ai.seo_question: How many prophets and trustees did God create according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* establishes the Shia doctrine of the parallel number of Prophets and their successors (Wasiyy), emphasizing the unique status of Imam Ali as the preeminent trustee. The chain of transmission highlights the direct lineage from the Prophet to Imam Ali through the Imams, reinforcing the concept of *Nass* (designation) in Twelver Shi'ism. This hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the spiritual hierarchy and continuity of divine guidance after the Prophet's era.
